meta.title: MotifJS — A live object tree, not a description
meta.description: MotifJS compiles JSX into code that builds component objects; no virtual tree, no template. Every element is an object with its DOM node, bindings and lifecycle. Routing and dependency injection with real scopes in one core.
about.title: About MotifJS
about.description: Every tag becomes a component object with its own element, children and bindings. There is no virtual tree and no template: the built element stays in your hands for the life of the application, and a state change writes to the node that reads it. Services with real scopes hold the state; there is no store to add.

home.preview.note: {state.count} compiles to a text binding; a click updates only that text node.
home.why.title: The view is built once.
home.why.description: After that the objects carry it. Bindings update values; the tree changes by hand or through bindings.
home.why.card1Title: Move it. Its state goes with it.
home.why.card1Description: Pass a component to another parent's controls.add and it leaves its old place with its state, bindings and events. detach plays the leave transition and keeps it for later.
home.why.card2Title: The tree is edited at run time.
home.why.card2Description: controls.add, insert, move, moveToIndex and remove change the component tree directly. On a built component, controls.add builds the child right away and puts its element in place; remove disposes it.
home.why.card3Title: Go back. It is the same page.
home.why.card3Description: A keepAlive route keeps its instance. With stack navigation, pages left behind stay for five steps by default and come back with their scroll positions; a slide transition and swipe-back are options.
home.why.card4Description: A disposed component shuts down its children, bindings and events; resources tied to it with motif.register or motif.setDisposable close with it; a subscription opened through context.on is removed on its own.
home.why.card5Description: Every route change opens its own service scope; a scoped service is created once per scope. When the next change completes, the previous scope closes with its services, unless a kept page still holds it.
home.why.card6Description: Routing, dependency injection, lifecycle, animation and memory management come with the core, along with Frame, Lazy, Transport, ContentBody, Virtualization, Resilience, Query and the List, Dictionary and LinkedList collections.
home.approach.title: JSX or plain code. Class, function or Options.
home.approach.description: A view is written in JSX or as the component calls JSX compiles to, in TypeScript or JavaScript. A component is a class, a function or an Options object. All three produce the same object.
home.approach.card1Title: JSX, or the calls it compiles to.
home.approach.card1Description: The compiler turns JSX into component calls. The same calls can be written by hand, and both can meet in one component: declare the view, then add or move controls at run time.
home.approach.card2Description: A function for a view with no state of its own; a class or an Options object when the component holds state and handles its lifecycle.
home.approach.card3Description: One reactive object per entity. Fill it in place and the bound nodes update; replace it and everything bound to it is rebuilt. Lists change through push and splice; a keyed row follows its item.
home.runtime.title: Browser, Electron, file://.
home.runtime.description: One application runs in all three. There is no server-side rendering.
home.runtime.point1: A component's element exists from the constructor, before it is built or mounted
home.runtime.point2: Router modes: history, hash, file, shell
home.runtime.point3: app.windows: a component in another window or in Picture-in-Picture, styles and theme mirrored
home.runtime.visualLabel: A reactive state value updates its bound DOM node
home.explore.title: In the core, not in add-ons.
home.explore.reactivityTitle: Reactive objects, signals, computed values, effects
home.explore.reactivityDescription: When a state field changes, only the DOM node or attribute bound to it is updated, not the component.
home.explore.routingTitle: Guards, redirects, lazy routes, nested views
home.explore.routingDescription: Route guards, redirect and alias, path parameters, lazy routes, nested and named RouterViews, kept pages.
home.explore.diDescription: Register with addSingleton, addScoped, addTransient or @Injectable; resolve with getService, inject, deps or FromService. A scoped service is reached through a handle that points to the right navigation.
home.explore.memoryDescription: An async result reaches a live component through using or doWork, or is dropped. DisposableStore groups what you open; detach, silentDetach and silentUnlink take a component out without disposing it. Leak tracking and live component counts in development.
home.explore.contentDescription: Frame swaps one changing piece of content. Lazy loads from a dynamic import or any Promise, with retries and cancellation. Transport shows content in a slot outside its own tree. Virtualization builds only the rows around the viewport.
home.explore.queryDescription: Query.from chains where, select, orderBy and groupBy. Resilience.create chains retry, timeout, circuit breaker, bulkhead, rate limiter and fallback. List, Dictionary and LinkedList ship with the core.
home.tooling.title: Checked at compile time and at run time.
home.tooling.card1Description: JSX mistakes are reported at build time with an MJX code; explain shows what each expression compiled to.
home.tooling.card2Description: app.useDevelopment(true) turns on warnings with MJX codes and route validation. The production build drops the line.
home.tooling.card3Description: Every error and warning carries a documented MJX code. Branch on the code, not on the message.
home.tooling.card4Description: A skill and llms.txt describe the framework to coding agents; npx skills add motifjsdev/skills installs it.
home.community.title: Open source, MIT licensed.
home.start.title: Install, add the plugin, mount.
home.start.description: Add the compiler's Vite plugin and mount a root component. Without a bundler, the UMD build runs from a script tag.
